      "content": "# ¿Cuál es la capital de Australia y qué la hace especial?

Cuando alguien pregunta cuál es la capital de Australia, la respuesta más habitual es Sydney o Melbourne. Sin embargo, ambas son erróneas. La capital de Australia es Canberra, una ciudad planificada desde cero a principios del siglo XX, construida expresamente para resolver una rivalidad histórica entre los dos mayores centros urbanos del país y que hoy alberga las principales instituciones del Estado federal australiano.

## Por qué Canberra es la capital y no Sydney o Melbourne

Para entender la elección de Canberra como capital es necesario remontarse al proceso de federación de Australia. En 1901, las seis colonias británicas que conformaban el continente se unificaron para crear la Mancomunidad de Australia, el actual Commonwealth of Australia. En el momento de redactar la Constitución, surgió de inmediato la pregunta inevitable: ¿dónde situar la capital del nuevo Estado federal?

Sydney, la ciudad más antigua y poblada, se creía con derecho natural a ser capital. Melbourne, la más próspera económicamente, no estaba dispuesta a ceder ese honor. El bloqueo político era total. La solución que acordaron los constituyentes fue ingeniosa y pragmática: la capital se construiría en un territorio nuevo, situado en Nueva Gales del Sur pero alejado al menos 160 kilómetros de Sydney, y ese territorio quedaría bajo jurisdicción federal directa.

### La elección del emplazamiento

Los ingenieros y geógrafos exploraron diversas localizaciones entre 1901 y 1908. El criterio fue encontrar un lugar con acceso a agua dulce suficiente, suelo apto para la construcción, un clima razonablemente moderado y la distancia reglamentaria de Sydney. La zona elegida fue el valle del río Molonglo, en las mesetas de las Montes Snowy, en el sureste del continente.

El Parlamento australiano aprobó en 1908 el Seat of Government Acceptance Act, que estableció formalmente el Territorio de la Capital Australiana (ACT, por sus siglas en inglés). Mientras tanto, Melbourne siguió siendo la sede provisional del gobierno federal hasta el traslado definitivo, que no se produciría hasta 1927.

## El concurso de diseño y los Griffin

En 1911, el gobierno federal convocó un concurso internacional de diseño urbano para la nueva capital. Se presentaron 137 proyectos procedentes de todo el mundo. El ganador fue el estudio del arquitecto estadounidense Walter Burley Griffin y su socia y esposa Marion Mahony Griffin, ambos discípulos de Frank Lloyd Wright en Chicago.

El diseño de los Griffin fue revolucionario para su época. Se trataba de una ciudad jardín de geometría radiocéntrica, con grandes avenidas que convergían en puntos nodales y cuya organización espacial estaba alineada con los accidentes topográficos del entorno: el Monte Ainslie, el Monte Bimberi, la Montaña Negra y la Colina del Capitolio. El centro cívico estaría articulado en torno a un lago artificial que se crearía represando el río Molonglo.

### El nombre de la ciudad

La ceremonia oficial de fundación tuvo lugar el 12 de marzo de 1913. Lady Denman, esposa del Gobernador General Lord Denman, anunció el nombre de la nueva capital en una ceremonia celebrada en la colina de Kurrajong, hoy conocida como Capital Hill. El nombre elegido fue "Canberra", una adaptación del término del idioma ngunnawal, el idioma de los pueblos aborígenes de la región. Su significado exacto es objeto de debate: las interpretaciones más citadas son "punto de encuentro" o "lugar donde la gente se reúne", aunque algunos lingüistas proponen otras traducciones relacionadas con una formación topográfica local.

## La construcción y el traslado del parlamento

El comienzo de la Primera Guerra Mundial en 1914 paralizó gran parte de los trabajos de construcción. El lago artificial que los Griffin habían previsto como corazón de la ciudad tardó décadas en materializarse: el lago Burley Griffin, llamado así en honor del arquitecto, no se inauguró hasta 1963.

El Parlamento de Australia se trasladó desde Melbourne a Canberra el 9 de mayo de 1927, en una ceremonia presidida por el duque de York, futuro rey Jorge VI. Durante décadas, el poder legislativo funcionó en el llamado Parlamento Provisional, un edificio que se construyó como solución temporal pero que terminó siendo utilizado durante sesenta y un años.

### La Casa del Parlamento actual

El edificio que actualmente alberga el Parlamento australiano se inauguró en 1988, con motivo del bicentenario de la colonización europea de Australia. Diseñado por el arquitecto italoestadounidense Romaldo Giurgola, está parcialmente construido bajo tierra en la cima de Capital Hill. Su asta de bandera, de 81 metros de altura, es visible desde casi cualquier punto de la ciudad y se ha convertido en el símbolo visual más reconocible de Canberra.

## Canberra hoy: datos y características

Con aproximadamente 370.000 habitantes, Canberra es la octava ciudad más grande de Australia y, en términos de riqueza per cápita, una de las más prósperas del país. Su economía está dominada por la administración pública federal, la educación universitaria y los institutos de investigación. La Universidad Nacional de Australia (ANU), fundada en 1946, es una de las instituciones académicas más prestigiosas del Pacífico.

La ciudad está organizada en una serie de distritos planificados separados por cinturones verdes, lo que le da un aspecto descentralizado y muy arbolado comparado con otras capitales. No tiene el skyline compacto de Sydney ni la vitalidad comercial de Melbourne, pero sus avenidas amplias, sus numerosos parques y su baja densidad de tráfico la convierten en una de las ciudades con mejor calidad de vida del mundo según varios índices internacionales.

### Clima de Canberra

El clima de Canberra es continental templado con cuatro estaciones bien definidas, algo inusual en el contexto australiano. Los veranos, de diciembre a febrero, son cálidos y secos, con temperaturas que pueden superar los 35 °C. Los inviernos son los más fríos del continente australiano, con heladas frecuentes y nevadas ocasionales, especialmente en los suburbios de mayor altitud. Las noches de julio pueden bajar de los 0 °C. Esta combinación climática es uno de los motivos por los que muchos australianos prefieren vivir en las ciudades costeras.

## Principales atractivos de Canberra

### El Triángulo Parlamentario

El núcleo cívico de Canberra es el llamado Triángulo Parlamentario, una zona delimitada por el lago Burley Griffin y las grandes avenidas del diseño original de los Griffin. En él se concentran los edificios del gobierno federal, los principales museos nacionales y la mayoría de los monumentos emblemáticos. La entrada es gratuita en prácticamente todos los museos, lo que convierte a Canberra en un destino extraordinariamente accesible para quien visite Australia con interés cultural.

Entre las instituciones más visitadas destacan el Museo Nacional de Australia, la Galería Nacional de Arte de Australia —con la mayor colección de arte del país—, la Biblioteca Nacional de Australia y el Instituto Australiano de Memoria de Guerra (Australian War Memorial), considerado uno de los mejores museos militares del mundo.

### El lago Burley Griffin

El lago artificial creado al represar el río Molonglo en 1963 es hoy el eje paisajístico y recreativo de la ciudad. Con una superficie de 664 hectáreas y un perímetro de 35 kilómetros, es un espacio para el ocio al aire libre, la navegación y el ciclismo. En el centro del lago se encuentra el Jet de la Commonwealth, una fuente que lanza agua a más de 147 metros de altura, siendo una de las más altas del mundo.

### El festival Floriade

Cada año, entre mediados de septiembre y mediados de octubre, el parque Commonwealth se llena de tulipanes y otras flores de primavera en el festival Floriade. Se trata de uno de los mayores festivales de flores del hemisferio sur, que atrae a visitantes de toda Australia y del extranjero.

## El debate sobre el papel de Canberra en la identidad australiana

A pesar de ser la capital federal, Canberra ocupa un lugar ambivalente en la identidad cultural australiana. La rivalidad histórica entre Sydney y Melbourne ha persistido hasta hoy, y muchos australianos bromean con que Canberra es una ciudad "artificial" o "burocrática" sin carácter propio. Sin embargo, los habitantes del Territorio de la Capital Australiana tienen un orgullo particular por su ciudad: sus museos de clase mundial, su vida universitaria activa, sus espacios naturales y su planificación urbana la diferencian claramente de cualquier otra gran ciudad del país.

Desde el punto de vista político, el ACT tiene un estatus especial dentro del sistema federal australiano: es un territorio con gobierno propio, no un Estado, lo que significa que tiene ciertas limitaciones en su autonomía legislativa respecto a los seis Estados federados. Cuenta con representación en el Parlamento federal y elige a sus propios legisladores, pero el gobierno federal puede, en principio, revocar su legislación.

## Preguntas frecuentes

### ¿Por qué mucha gente cree que la capital de Australia es Sydney?

Sydney es la ciudad más grande, más conocida internacionialmente y la que más aparece en los medios de comunicación globales. Además, alberga la sede de muchas empresas multinacionales, el puerto más famoso del país y el puente y la ópera que son los símbolos visuales de Australia en el exterior. Esa visibilidad hace que muchos asocien Sydney con el papel de capital, aunque políticamente ese rol corresponde a Canberra.

### ¿Cuándo se convirtió Canberra oficialmente en capital de Australia?

El nombre "Canberra" fue anunciado oficialmente el 12 de marzo de 1913. Sin embargo, el traslado real del gobierno federal desde Melbourne no se produjo hasta el 9 de mayo de 1927, cuando se inauguró el edificio parlamentario provisional y se celebró la primera sesión del Parlamento en la nueva capital.

### ¿Qué significa el nombre "Canberra"?

El nombre proviene de la lengua ngunnawal, el idioma de los pueblos aborígenes que habitaban la región. La traducción más aceptada es "lugar de encuentro" o "punto donde la gente se reúne", aunque existe debate entre lingüistas sobre el significado preciso. Algunas fuentes lo vinculan también a la expresión "ceno berri", que podría referirse a los senos de la mujer en relación con las formas del terreno.

### ¿Es Canberra una ciudad segura para vivir o visitar?

Canberra figura sistemáticamente entre las ciudades más seguras de Australia y del mundo en los índices internacionales de calidad de vida. Sus índices de criminalidad son bajos, sus infraestructuras están bien mantenidas y su sistema de transporte público, aunque mejorable comparado con ciudades europeas, cubre las zonas principales. Es una ciudad recomendable tanto para residir como para visitar.

### ¿Qué diferencia al Territorio de la Capital Australiana de los estados australianos?

El ACT no es un Estado sino un Territorio federal, lo que implica que su gobierno tiene menos autonomía legislativa. A diferencia de los seis Estados australianos, que tienen poderes residuales amplios, el Territorio puede ver su legislación enmendada o derogada por el Parlamento federal. Comparte esa condición con el Territorio del Norte, aunque ambos tienen parlamentos propios y cierta capacidad de autogobierno.

### ¿Vale la pena visitar Canberra como turista?

Sí, especialmente para quienes tienen interés en la historia, el arte o la política australiana. Sus museos nacionales son de entrada gratuita y de altísimo nivel, el lago Burley Griffin ofrece un entorno agradable para pasear, y la zona del Triángulo Parlamentario tiene una escala humana que la hace fácilmente explorable a pie. **Canberra** ([//](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English) [ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-au-Canberra-ACT.ogg)[*KAN-brə*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key); [Ngunawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunawal_language): *Kanbarra*) is the [capital city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city) of [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia) and the largest population centre in the [Australian Capital Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory). With an estimated population of 484,630 as of 2025, Canberra is Australia's [largest inland city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Australia) and the [eighth-largest Australian city by population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population). The city occupies most of the northern quadrant of the Australian Capital Territory, and its urban sprawl borders the state of [New South Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales) to the northwest, northeast and southeast. The [Brindabellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindabella_Range) are located south and west of the city, and form the northern part of the [Australian Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Alps), the country's highest mountain range.

Canberra was established following the [federation of the Australian colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia) to serve as the seat of government for the new nation, being a compromise between [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney) and [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne), Australia’s two largest cities. The area chosen for the capital had been inhabited by [Aboriginal Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians) for up to 21,000 years, by groups including the [Ngunnawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunnawal) and [Ngambri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngambri). [European settlement](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Australia_(1788–1850)>) commenced in the first half of the 19th century, evidenced by surviving landmarks such as [St John's Anglican Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_John_the_Baptist_Church,_Reid) and [Blundells Cottage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blundells_Cottage). On 1 January 1901, federation of the colonies of Australia was achieved. The capital city was founded and formally named as Canberra in 1913. Unusual among Australian cities, it is an entirely [planned city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_community), grounded in a design by [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States) architects [Walter Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Burley_Griffin) and [Marion Mahony Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Mahony_Griffin). The Griffins' plan was influenced by the [garden city movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_city_movement) and featured geometric motifs aligned with significant topographical landmarks such as [Black Mountain](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mountain_(Australian_Capital_Territory)>), [Mount Ainslie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Ainslie), [Capital Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_Hill,_Australian_Capital_Territory) and [City Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Hill,_Canberra). Its design can be viewed from its highest point at the [Telstra Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telstra_Tower) and the summit of Mount Ainslie. Other notable features include the [National Arboretum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Arboretum_Canberra) and [Lake Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Burley_Griffin).

As the seat of the [Government of Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Australia), Canberra is home to many important institutions of the federal government, national monuments and museums. These include [Parliament House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_House,_Canberra), [Government House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_House,_Canberra), the [High Court building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Australia_Building) and the headquarters of numerous government agencies. Social and cultural institutions of national significance include the [Australian War Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_War_Memorial), the [Australian National University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_National_University), the [Royal Australian Mint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Australian_Mint), the [Australian Institute of Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Institute_of_Sport), the [National Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gallery_of_Australia), the [National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Australia) and the [National Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Australia). The city is home to many important institutions of the [Australian Defence Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Defence_Force) including the [Royal Military College Duntroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_College,_Duntroon) and the [Australian Defence Force Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Defence_Force_Academy). It hosts [all foreign embassies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_in_Australia#Diplomatic_missions_in_Canberra) in Australia as well as regional headquarters of many international organisations, not-for-profit groups, lobbying groups and professional associations.

Canberra has been ranked among the world's best cities to live in and visit. Compared to the national averages, the unemployment rate is lower and the average income higher; tertiary education levels are higher, while the population is younger. At the 2021 Census, 28.7% of Canberra's inhabitants were reported as having been born overseas. The [Australian Public Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Public_Service) accounted for about 25% all jobs as at November 2025. Other major industries include health care, professional services, education and training, retail, accommodation and food, and construction. Annual cultural events include [Floriade](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floriade_(Canberra)>), the largest flower festival in the Southern Hemisphere, the [Enlighten Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlighten_Canberra), [Skyfire](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyfire_(Canberra)>), the [National Multicultural Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Multicultural_Festival) and [Summernats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summernats). Canberra's main sporting venues are [Canberra Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Stadium) and [Manuka Oval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuka_Oval). The city is served with domestic and international flights at [Canberra Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Airport), while interstate train and coach services depart from [Canberra railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_railway_station) and the [Jolimont Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolimont_Centre) respectively. [City Interchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Interchange) and [Alinga Street station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alinga_Street_light_rail_station) form the hub of Canberra's bus and light rail transport network.

## Name

The word "Canberra" is derived from the [Ngunnawal language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunnawal_language) of a local [Ngunnawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunnawal) or [Ngambri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngambri) clan who resided in the area and were referred to by the early British colonists as either the *Canberry*, *Kanberri* or *Nganbra* tribe.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:9-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-11)[Joshua John Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_John_Moore), the first European land-owner in the region, named his grant "Canberry" in 1823 after these people. "Canberry Creek" and "Canberry" first appeared on regional maps from 1830, while the derivative name "Canberra" started to appear from around 1857.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-selkirk-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-13)<sup>[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-14)</sup> Other early recorded variants of the spelling include "Canbury" (potentially influenced by [the settlement of the same name in England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canbury)), "Canburry" and "Kembery".[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-15)

Numerous local commentators, including the Ngunnawal elder Don Bell, have speculated upon possible meanings of "Canberra" over the years. These include "meeting place", "woman's breasts" and "the hollow between a woman's breasts".[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Frei-16)<sup>[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-17)</sup> References to breasts or [the space between them](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleavage_(breasts)>) are thought to derive from [Black Mountain](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mountain_(Australian_Capital_Territory)>) and [Mount Ainslie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Ainslie), two large hills with similar elevations situated immediately to the northwest and northeast, respectively, of what is now [the city centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civic,_Australian_Capital_Territory).[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-20)

Alternative proposals for the name of the city during its planning included Austral, Australville, Aurora, Captain Cook, Caucus City, Cookaburra, Dampier, Eden, Eucalypta, Flinders, Gonebroke, Home, Hopetoun, Kangaremu, Myola, Meladneyperbane, New Era, Olympus, Paradise, Shakespeare, Sydmelperadbrisho, Swindleville, The National City, Union City, Unison, Wattleton, Wheatwoolgold, Yass-Canberra.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-21)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-23)

## History

### First Nations peoples

The first peoples of the Canberra area include the [Ngunnawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngunnawal), Ngunawal and [Ngambri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngambri) peoples.<sup>[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:8-24)</sup> Other groups claiming a connection to the land include the [Ngarigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngarigo) (who also lived directly to the south) and the Ngambri-Guumaal.<sup>[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:9-10)</sup> Neighbouring groups include the Wandandian to the east, the Walgulu also to the south, [Gandangara people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandangara_people) to the north and [Wiradjuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiradjuri) to the north-west.

The first British settlers into the Canberra area described two clans of Ngunnawal people resident to the vicinity. The *Canberry* or *Nganbra* clan lived mostly around Sullivan's Creek and had ceremonial grounds at the base of Galambary ([Black Mountain](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mountain_(Australian_Capital_Territory)>)), while the *Pialligo* clan had land around what is now [Canberra Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Airport).[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bluett-25)<sup>[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-26)</sup> The people living here carefully managed and cultivated the land with fire, farmed yams, and hunted for food.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:7-27)

Archaeological evidence of settlement in the region includes inhabited rock shelters, rock paintings and engravings, burial places, camps and quarry sites as well as stone tools and arrangements.<sup>[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Gillespie84-28)</sup> Artefacts suggests early human activity occurred at some point in the area 21,000 years previously.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:1-29)

Still today, Ngunnawal men into the present conduct ceremony on the banks of the river, Murrumbidgee River. They travel upstream as they receive their Totems and corresponding responsibilities for land management. 'Murrum' means 'Pathway' and Bidgee means 'Boss'.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:7-27)

The submerged limestone caves beneath Lake Burley Griffin contained Aboriginal rock art, some of the only sites in the region.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:7-27)

Galambary (Black Mountain) is an important Aboriginal meeting and business site, predominantly for men's business. According to the Ngunnawal and [Ngambri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngambri) people, Mt Ainslie is primarily for place of women's business. Black Mountain and Mount Ainslie are referred to as women's breasts. Galambary was also used by Ngunnawal people as an initiation site, with the mountain itself said to represent the growth of a boy into a man.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:7-27)

### British exploration and colonisation

In October 1820, [Charles Throsby Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Throsby_Smith) led the first British expedition to the area.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-cambage-31)[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-32)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald19875-33)<sup>[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie19913–8-34)</sup> Four other expeditions occurred between 1820 and 1823 with the first accurate map being produced by explorer [Mark John Currie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_John_Currie) in June 1823. By this stage, the area had become known as the Limestone Plains.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-cambage-31)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-35)

British settlement of the area probably dates from late 1823, when a [sheep station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep_station) was formed on what is now the Acton Peninsula by James Cowan, the head stockman employed by [Joshua John Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_John_Moore).<sup>[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie19919-36)</sup> Moore had received a land grant in the region in 1823 and formally applied to purchase the site on 16 December 1826. He named the property "Canberry". On 30 April 1827, Moore was told by letter that he could retain possession of 1,000 acres (405 ha) at Canberry.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-37)

Other colonists soon followed Moore's example to take up land in the region. Around 1825, [James Ainslie](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Ainslie_(pastoralist)>), working on behalf of the wealthy merchant [Robert Campbell](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Campbell_(1769–1846)>), arrived to establish a sheep station. He was guided to the region by a local Aboriginal girl who showed him the fine lands of her *Pialligo* clan.<sup>[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bluett-25)</sup> The area then became the property of Campbell and it was initially named [Pialligo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pialligo,_Australian_Capital_Territory) before Campbell changed it to the Scottish title of [Duntroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duntroon,_Australian_Capital_Territory).[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-selkirk-12)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney198848-38)<sup>[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald19879-39)</sup> Campbell and his family built a [dairy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dairy) on the site in 1832, now regarded as the oldest standing European building in Canberra,[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-40)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-41)<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-42)</sup> followed by the imposing stone house that is now the officers' mess of the [Royal Military College, Duntroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_College,_Duntroon).<sup>[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-43)</sup> The Campbells sponsored settlement by other farmer families to work their land, such as the Southwells of "[Weetangera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weetangera,_Australian_Capital_Territory)".[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney198887–95-44)

Other notable early colonists included Henry Donnison, who established the [Yarralumla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yarralumla,_Australian_Capital_Territory) estate—now the site of the [official residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_House,_Canberra) of the [Governor-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General) of Australia—in 1827, and John Palmer who employed Duncan Macfarlane to form the [Jerrabomberra](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerrabomberra_(district)>) property in 1828. A year later, John MacPherson established the [Springbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springbank_Island) estate, becoming the first British owner-occupier in the region.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-selkirk-12)[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-45)[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-46)

The Anglican church of [St John the Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_John_the_Baptist_Church,_Reid), in the suburb of Reid,<sup>[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988116-47)</sup> was consecrated in 1845, and is now the oldest surviving public building in the city.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie199178-48)<sup>[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198717-49)</sup> St John's churchyard contains the earliest graves in the district.<sup>[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-50)</sup> It has been described as a "sanctuary in the city",[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-51)<sup>[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-52)</sup> remaining a small English village-style church even as the capital grew around it. Canberra's first school, St John's School (now a museum), was situated next to the church and opened in the same year of 1845.<sup>[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-53)</sup> It was built to educate local settlers children,<sup>[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Nohra-54)</sup> including the Blundell children who lived in nearby [Blundell's Cottage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blundell's_Cottage).[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Sue_W-55)

As the European presence increased, the Indigenous population dwindled largely due to the destruction of their society, dislocation from their lands and from introduced diseases such as [influenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Influenza), [smallpox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox), [alcoholism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcoholism), and [measles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles).[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-56)[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-canb-57)

The district's change from a rural area in New South Wales to the national capital started during debates over [federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia) in the late 19th century.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198792-58)<sup>[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie1991220–230-59)</sup> Following a long dispute over whether Sydney or Melbourne should be the national capital,<sup>[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:2-60)</sup> a compromise was reached: the new capital would be built in New South Wales, so long as it was at least 100 mi (160 km) from Sydney,<sup>[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198792-58)</sup> with Melbourne to be the temporary seat of government while the new capital was built.<sup>[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore197124-61)</sup> A survey was conducted across several sites in New South Wales with [Bombala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombala), southern [Monaro](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaro_(New_South_Wales)>), [Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange,_New_South_Wales), [Yass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yass,_New_South_Wales), [Albury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albury), [Tamworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamworth,_New_South_Wales), [Armidale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armidale), [Tumut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumut), and [Dalgety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalgety,_New_South_Wales) all discussed.<sup>[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-62)</sup> Dalgety was chosen by the federal parliament and it passed the *[Seat of Government Act 1904](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seat_of_Government_Act_1904)* confirming Dalgety as the site of the nation's capital. However, the New South Wales government refused to cede the required territory as they did not accept the site.<sup>[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-62)</sup> In 1906, the New South Wales Government finally agreed to cede sufficient land provided that it was in the Yass-Canberra region as this site was closer to Sydney.<sup>[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198792-58)</sup> Newspaper proprietor [John Gale](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Gale_(journalist)>) circulated a pamphlet titled 'Dalgety or Canberra: Which?' advocating Canberra to every member of the Commonwealth's seven state and federal parliaments. By many accounts, it was decisive in the selection of Canberra as the site in 1908 as was a result of survey work done by the government [surveyor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surveying) [Charles Scrivener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Scrivener).<sup>[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198793-63)</sup> The NSW government ceded the district to the federal government in 1911 and the [Federal Capital Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory) was established.[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald198792-58)

An international design competition was launched by the Department of Home Affairs on 30 April 1911, closing on 31 January 1912. The competition was boycotted by the [Royal Institute of British Architects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_British_Architects), the [Institution of Civil Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institution_of_Civil_Engineers) and their affiliated bodies throughout the British Empire because the Minister for Home Affairs [King O'Malley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_O'Malley) insisted that the final decision was for him to make rather than an expert in city planning.<sup>[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-tom-64)</sup> A total of 137 valid entries were received. O'Malley appointed a three-member board to advise him but they could not reach unanimity. On 24 May 1911,<sup>[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987100-65)</sup> O'Malley came down on the side of the majority of the board with the design by [Walter Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Burley_Griffin) and [Marion Mahony Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Mahony_Griffin) of [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago), Illinois, United States, being declared the winner.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie1991178-66)<sup>[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore1971160–166-67)</sup> Second was [Eliel Saarinen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliel_Saarinen) of Finland and third was [Alfred Agache](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Agache_(architect)>) of Brazil but resident in Paris, France.<sup>[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-tom-64)</sup> O'Malley then appointed a six-member board to advise him on the implementation of the winning design. On 25 November 1912, the board advised that it could not support the Griffins' plan in its entirety and suggested an alternative plan of its own devising. This plan ostensibly incorporated the best features of the three place-getting designs as well as of a fourth design by H. Caswell, R.C.G. Coulter and W. Scott-Griffiths of Sydney, the rights to which it had purchased. It was this composite plan that was endorsed by Parliament and given formal approval by O'Malley on 10 January 1913.<sup>[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-tom-64)</sup> However, it was the Griffin plan which was ultimately proceeded with. In 1913, Walter Burley Griffin was appointed Federal Capital Director of Design and Construction and construction began.<sup>[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore197163-68)</sup> On 23 February, King O'Malley drove the first peg in the construction of the future capital city.

In 1912, the government invited suggestions from the public as to the name of the future city. Almost 750 names were suggested. At midday on 12 March 1913,[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGillespie1991303-69)[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-70)[Lady Denman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gertrude_Denman,_Baroness_Denman), the wife of Governor-General [Lord Denman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Denman,_3rd_Baron_Denman), announced that the city would be named "Canberra" at a ceremony at Kurrajong Hill,[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987103-71)[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAustralian_Bureau_of_Statistics1963-72)<sup>[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-73)</sup> which has since become Capital Hill and the site of the present [Parliament House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_House,_Canberra).[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987105-74)[Canberra Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Day) is a public holiday observed in the ACT on the second Monday in March to celebrate the founding of Canberra.<sup>[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-canb-57)</sup> After the ceremony, bureaucratic disputes hindered Griffin's work;<sup>[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore197170–71-75)</sup> a Royal Commission in 1916 ruled his authority had been usurped by certain officials and his original plan was reinstated.<sup>[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987101-76)</sup> Griffin's relationship with the Australian authorities was strained and a lack of funding meant that by the time he was fired in 1920, little work had been done.[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTENational_Capital_Development_Commission19884-77)<sup>[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore197169–79-78)</sup> By this time, Griffin had revised his plan, overseen the earthworks of major avenues and established the Glenloch Cork Plantation.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-act-79)[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-80)

### Development throughout 20th century

The Commonwealth government purchased the pastoral property of [Yarralumla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_House,_Canberra) in 1913 to provide an official residence for the Governor-General of Australia in the new capital.<sup>[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Australiana_Fund-81)</sup> Renovations began in 1925 to enlarge and modernise the property.<sup>[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-82)</sup> In 1927, the property was officially dubbed Government House.<sup>[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Australiana_Fund-81)</sup> On 9 May that year, the Commonwealth parliament moved to Canberra with the opening of the [Provisional Parliament House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Parliament_House,_Canberra).[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987130-83)<sup>[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-84)</sup> The [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia) [Stanley Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Bruce) had officially taken up residence in [The Lodge](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lodge_(Australia)>) a few days earlier.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-85)<sup>[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore1971101-86)</sup> Planned development of the city slowed significantly during the [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_Australia) of the 1930s and during World War II.<sup>[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore1971125–128-87)</sup> Some projects planned for that time, including [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholicism_in_Australia) and [Anglican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Church_of_Australia) cathedrals, were never completed.<sup>[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988116–126-88)</sup> (Nevertheless, in 1973 the Roman Catholic parish church of St. Christopher was remodelled into [St Christopher's Cathedral, Manuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Christopher's_Cathedral,_Manuka), serving the Archdiocese of Canberra and Goulburn. It is the only cathedral in Canberra.<sup>[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-89)</sup>)

From 1920 to 1957, three bodies — successively the [Federal Capital Advisory Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Capital_Advisory_Committee),<sup>[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987115-90)</sup> the [Federal Capital Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Capital_Commission),<sup>[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987128-91)</sup> and the [National Capital Planning and Development Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Planning_and_Development_Committee) — continued to plan the further expansion of Canberra in the absence of Griffin. However, they were only advisory and development decisions were made without consulting them, which increased inefficiency.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-act-79)[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore1971113-92)

The largest event in Canberra up to World War II was the 24th Meeting of [ANZAAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANZAAS) in January 1939. *[The Canberra Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Canberra_Times)* described it as "a signal event ... in the history of this, the world's youngest capital city". The city's accommodation was not nearly sufficient to house the 1,250 delegates and a tent city had to be set up on the banks of the Molonglo River. One of the prominent speakers was [H. G. Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._G._Wells), who was a guest of the Governor-General [Lord Gowrie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Hore-Ruthven,_1st_Earl_of_Gowrie) for a week. This event coincided with a heatwave across south-eastern Australia during which the temperature in Canberra reached 108.5 degrees Fahrenheit (42.5 Celsius) on 11 January. On Friday, 13 January, the [Black Friday bushfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Friday_bushfires) caused 71 deaths in Victoria and Wells accompanied the Governor-General on his tour of areas threatened by fires.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-93)

Immediately after the end of the war, Canberra was criticised for resembling a village and its disorganised collection of buildings was deemed ugly.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke19886-94)[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke19881–3-95)<sup>[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke19887–9-96)</sup> Canberra was often derisively described as "several suburbs in search of a city".<sup>[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-97)</sup> Prime Minister [Sir Robert Menzies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Robert_Menzies) regarded the state of the national capital as an embarrassment.<sup>[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke198830-98)</sup> Over time his attitude changed from one of contempt to that of championing its development. He fired two ministers charged with the development of the city for poor performance. Menzies remained in office for over a decade and in that time the development of the capital sped up rapidly.[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke198831–32-99)<sup>[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988103–104,_145,_188,_323-100)</sup> The population grew by more than 50 per cent in every five-year period from 1955 to 1975.<sup>[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988103–104,_145,_188,_323-100)</sup> Several Government departments, together with public servants, were moved to Canberra from Melbourne following the war.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWigmore1971111–120-101)[Government housing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_housing_in_the_Australian_Capital_Territory) projects were undertaken to accommodate the city's growing population.[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988230–242-102)

The [National Capital Development Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Capital_Development_Commission) (NCDC) formed in 1957 with executive powers and ended four decades of disputes over the shape and design of [Lake Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Burley_Griffin) — the centrepiece of Griffin's design — and construction was completed in 1964 after four years of work.<sup>[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988130–140-103)</sup> The completion of the lake finally laid the platform for the development of Griffin's [Parliamentary Triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_Triangle,_Canberra).<sup>[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988170–180-104)</sup> Since the initial construction of the lake, various buildings of national importance have been constructed on its shores.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTENational_Capital_Development_Commission198818-105)

The newly built [Australian National University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_National_University) was expanded and sculptures as well as monuments were built.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTENational_Capital_Development_Commission198818-105)<sup>[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988173–174-106)</sup> A new [National Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Australia) was constructed within the Parliamentary Triangle, followed by the [High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Court_of_Australia) and the [National Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gallery_of_Australia).[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988116-47)<sup>[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987138-107)</sup> Suburbs in [Canberra Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Central) (often referred to as [North Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Canberra) and [South Canberra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Canberra)) were further developed in the 1950s and urban development in the [districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburbs_of_Canberra#Districts) of [Woden Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woden_Valley) and [Belconnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belconnen) commenced in the mid and late 1960s respectively, followed by the district of [Tuggeranong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuggeranong) in the mid-1970s.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988250-108)[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988180-109)<sup>[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-110)</sup> Many of the new suburbs were named after Australian politicians such as [Barton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Barton), [Deakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Deakin), [Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Reid), [Braddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Braddon), [Curtin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Curtin), [Chifley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Chifley) and [Parkes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Parkes).[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEUniversal_Publishers20076-111)

On 9 May 1988, a larger and permanent Parliament House was opened on Capital Hill as part of Australia's bicentenary celebrations.[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-pho-112)<sup>[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFitzgerald1987138-107)</sup> The Commonwealth Parliament moved there from the Provisional Parliament House, now known as Old Parliament House.[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-pho-112)

### Self-government

In December 1988, the Australian Capital Territory was granted full self-government by the Commonwealth Parliament, a step proposed as early as 1965.<sup>[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-113)</sup> Following the first election on 4 March 1989,<sup>[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-114)</sup> a 17-member [Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Capital_Territory_Legislative_Assembly) sat at temporary offices at 1 Constitution Avenue, Civic, on 11 May 1989.[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-115)<sup>[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-ass-116)</sup> Permanent premises were opened on London Circuit in 1994.<sup>[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-ass-116)</sup> The [Australian Labor Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Labor_Party) formed the ACT's first government, led by the Chief Minister [Rosemary Follett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Follett), who made history as Australia's first female head of government.[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-state_el-117)<sup>[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-118)</sup> The 1990s also saw urban development begin in the district of [Gungahlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gungahlin) in the far north of the ACT.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-119)[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-120)

Parts of Canberra were engulfed by [bushfires on 18 January 2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_Canberra_bushfires) that killed four people, injured 435 and destroyed more than 500 homes as well as the major research telescopes of Australian National University's [Mount Stromlo Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Stromlo_Observatory).[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Doogan-121)

Throughout 2013, several events celebrated the 100th anniversary of the naming of Canberra.<sup>[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-122)</sup> On 11 March 2014, the last day of the centennial year, the [Canberra Centenary Column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra_Centenary_Column) was unveiled in [City Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Hill). Other works included *[The Skywhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Skywhale)*, a hot air balloon designed by the sculptor [Patricia Piccinini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Piccinini),<sup>[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-123)</sup> and *StellrScope* by visual media artist Eleanor Gates-Stuart.<sup>[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-124)</sup> On 7 February 2021, *The Skywhale* was joined by *Skywhalepapa* to create a *Skywhale family*, an event marked by Skywhale-themed pastries and beer produced by local companies as well as an [art pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_pop) song entitled "We are the Skywhales".[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-ABC_2021_New_Skywhale_hot_air_balloon-125)

In 2014, Canberra was named the best city to live in the world by the [Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OECD),[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:3-126)[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-127)<sup>[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-128)</sup> and was named the third best city to visit in the world by [Lonely Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonely_Planet) in 2017.[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:4-129)[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:5-130)

## Geography

Canberra is located near the [Brindabella Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindabella_Ranges) (part of the [Australian Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Alps)), approximately 150 km (93 mi) inland from [Australia's east coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_Australia). Canberra is not incorporated, but its urban environs, which include a large part of the ACT east of the [Murrumbidgee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrumbidgee_River), have an elevation of approximately 580 m (1,900 ft) [AHD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Height_Datum);<sup>[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)</sup> the highest point near the built up area is [Mount Majura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Majura) at 888 m (2,913 ft).[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-132)<sup>[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-133)</sup> Other low mountains include [Mount Taylor](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Taylor_(Australian_Capital_Territory)>) 855 m (2,805 ft),[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-134)[Mount Ainslie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Ainslie) 843 m (2,766 ft),<sup>[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-135)</sup> Mount Mugga Mugga 812 m (2,664 ft)<sup>[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-136)</sup> and [Black Mountain](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Mountain_(Australian_Capital_Territory)>) 812 m (2,664 ft).[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-137)[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPenguin_Books_Australia200028-138)

The native forest in the Canberra region was almost wholly [eucalypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucalyptus) species and provided a resource for fuel and domestic purposes. By the early 1960s, logging had depleted the eucalypt, and concern about water quality led to the forests being closed. Interest in forestry began in 1915 with trials of a number of species including *[Pinus radiata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_radiata)* on the slopes of Mount Stromlo. Since then, plantations have been expanded, with the benefit of reducing erosion in the Cotter catchment, and the forests are also popular recreation areas.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-139)

The urban environs of Canberra straddle the [Ginninderra plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginninderra), [Molonglo plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molonglo_plain), the Limestone plain, and the [Tuggeranong plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuggeranong) (Isabella's Plain).<sup>[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988inside_cover-140)</sup> The [Molonglo River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molonglo_River) which flows across the Molonglo plain has been dammed to form the national capital's iconic feature [Lake Burley Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Burley_Griffin).<sup>[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988131–132-141)</sup> The Molonglo then flows into the [Murrumbidgee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murrumbidgee_River) north-west of Canberra, which in turn flows north-west toward the New South Wales town of Yass. The [Queanbeyan River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queanbeyan_River) joins the Molonglo River at Oaks Estate just within the ACT.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988inside_cover-140)

A number of creeks, including Jerrabomberra and Yarralumla Creeks, flow into the Molonglo and Murrumbidgee.<sup>[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGibbney1988inside_cover-140)</sup> Two of these creeks, the Ginninderra and Tuggeranong, have similarly been dammed to form Lakes [Ginninderra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ginninderra) and [Tuggeranong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Tuggeranong).[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke1988181–182-142)[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-143)<sup>[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWilliams2006260-144)</sup> Until recently the Molonglo River had a history of sometimes calamitous floods; the area was a flood plain prior to the filling of Lake Burley Griffin.[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-FOOTNOTESparke19884–7,_13–14-145)[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-NCA_Scrivener-146)

### Climate

Under the [Köppen-Geiger classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Köppen_climate_classification), Canberra has an [oceanic climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanic_climate) (*Cfb*).<sup>[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-147)</sup> In January, the warmest month, the average high is approximately 29 °C (84 °F); in July, the coldest month, the average high drops to approximately 12 °C (54 °F).

Frost is common in the winter months. Snow is rare in the CBD (central business district) due to being on the [leeward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward) (eastern) side of the dividing range, but the surrounding areas get annual snowfall through winter and often the snow-capped [Brindabella Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindabella_Range) can be seen from the CBD. The last significant snowfall in the city centre was in 1968.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)

The highest recorded maximum temperature was 44.0 °C (111.2 °F) on 4 January 2020.<sup>[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-148)</sup> Winter 2011 was Canberra's warmest winter on record, approximately 2 °C (4 °F) above the average temperature.<sup>[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-149)</sup> The lowest recorded minimum temperature was −10.0 °C (14.0 °F) on the morning of 11 July 1971.<sup>[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)</sup> Light snow falls only once in every few years, and is usually not widespread and quickly dissipates.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)

Canberra is protected from the west by the [Brindabellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brindabellas) which create a strong [rain shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_shadow) in Canberra's valleys.<sup>[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)</sup> Canberra gets 100.4 clear days annually.<sup>[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-autogenerated1-150)</sup> Annual rainfall is the third lowest of the capital cities (after [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide) and [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart))<sup>[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-151)</sup> and is spread fairly evenly over the seasons, with late spring bringing the highest rainfall.[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-152)[Thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorm) occur mostly between October and April, owing to the effect of summer and the mountains.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)

The area is generally [sheltered from a westerly wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Australian_foehn), though strong northwesterlies can develop. A cool, vigorous afternoon easterly change, colloquially referred to as a 'sea-breeze' or the 'Braidwood Butcher',[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-153)<sup>[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-154)</sup> is common during the summer months<sup>[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-155)</sup> and often exceeds 40 km/h in the city. Canberra is also less humid than the nearby coastal areas.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-bom-131)

Canberra was severely affected by smoke haze during the [2019/2020 bushfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Australian_bushfire_season). On 1 January 2020, Canberra had the worst air quality of any major city in the world, with an AQI of 7700 (USAQI 949).[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-156)

## ¿La capital de Australia es Sydney o Canberra?

La capital de Australia es Canberra, no Sydney. Este es uno de los errores más extendidos sobre el país. Sydney es la ciudad más grande y más famosa de Australia, pero nunca ha sido la capital oficial. Cuando los estados australianos se federaron en 1901, ni Sydney ni Melbourne consiguieron el título. Construyeron una ciudad nueva, Canberra, que se convirtió en la capital en 1927 cuando el Parlamento se instaló allí. Hoy Canberra alberga el Parlamento, el gobierno federal, la mayoría de las embajadas extranjeras y las instituciones nacionales más importantes del país.

## ¿Qué idioma se habla en Canberra?

En Canberra se habla inglés, concretamente inglés australiano. Es el idioma oficial y el que se usa en todos los ámbitos: trabajo, educación, administración pública y vida cotidiana. Sin embargo, Canberra es una ciudad con una presencia diplomática e internacional muy significativa. Hay más de 90 embajadas y altas comisiones extranjeras establecidas en la ciudad, lo que hace que escuches decenas de idiomas en la calle. También existe una comunidad hispanohablante activa, especialmente entre universitarios y trabajadores del sector público con perfiles internacionales.

## ¿Cómo es la vida en Canberra, Australia?

La vida en Canberra es tranquila, ordenada y con una calidad de vida muy alta. Es una ciudad mediana (unos 450.000 habitantes) con todos los servicios de una gran ciudad pero sin el caos de Sydney o Melbourne. Los salarios son los más altos de Australia (gracias al empleo público federal), el desempleo es el más bajo del país y el acceso a naturaleza es excepcional: parques nacionales, lago Burley Griffin, montañas nevadas en invierno. El lado negativo: la vida nocturna es limitada, el coche es casi necesario y los inviernos son fríos de verdad, con heladas y temperaturas bajo cero por las noches.

## ¿Cuál era la capital de Australia antes de Canberra?

Antes de Canberra, la capital provisional de Australia fue Melbourne. Cuando la Commonwealth de Australia se proclamó en 1901, tanto Sydney como Melbourne querían ser la capital, pero ninguna cedió. La solución fue establecer Melbourne como sede provisional del Parlamento mientras se construía Canberra en un territorio neutral. Melbourne ejerció como capital de facto durante 26 años, desde 1901 hasta 1927, cuando el Parlamento australiano se trasladó definitivamente a Canberra.

## ¿Se dice Canberra o Camberra?

Las dos formas son aceptadas en español, aunque la grafía original en inglés es Canberra. En Australia siempre encontrarás la forma inglesa: Canberra. La versión hispanizada «Camberra» aparece en algunos textos en español, incluida la Wikipedia en castellano, pero hoy en día la mayoría de medios y hablantes en español usan directamente Canberra.
